paper_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the tandem organic solar cell utilizing the PNDIT-F3N:PEI/PEDOT:PSS interconnecting layer?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimized tandem organic solar cell achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 12.6%. When measured without an aperture, the device reached a PCE of 13.2%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: Which materials constitute the electron transport layer (ETL) and the hole transport layer (HTL) within the interconnecting layer (ICL) of this tandem device?
qa_pairs.answer: The interconnecting layer (ICL) consists of a blend of PNDIT-F3N and poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) as the electron transport layer (ETL), which is paired with PEDOT:PSS as the hole transport layer (HTL).
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: How does the incorporation of poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) into the PNDIT-F3N matrix influence the work function of the modified PEDOT:PSS?
qa_pairs.answer: The work function (WF) of PEDOT:PSS modified by the PNDIT-F3N:PEI blend can be linearly tuned by adjusting the ratio of PEI. It decreases from 4.43 eV when using pure PNDIT-F3N to 3.75 eV with pure PEI, due to the large amount of amine groups on the PEI chain.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: Describe the composition and spectral coverage of the front and back subcells in the reported tandem organic solar cell.
qa_pairs.answer: The tandem device features a wide-bandgap front cell composed of PSTzBI-EHp:PC71BM and a narrow-bandgap back cell composed of PBDTTT-E-T:IEICO. This combination allows the device to harvest photons across a broad spectral range from 300 to 920 nm.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: What is the primary advantage of using methanol as a processing solvent for the PNDIT-F3N:PEI electron transport layer?
qa_pairs.answer: Methanol is an environmentally friendly solvent in which both PNDIT-F3N and PEI show excellent solubility. Its use prevents the erosion or dissolution of the underlying active layer and the subsequent PEDOT:PSS layer during the solution-processing of the device.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: Based on the transfer matrix method modeling, what are the optimal thicknesses for the front and back subcells to maximize the short-circuit current density (Jsc)?
qa_pairs.answer: The optical modeling predicted that the optimal thickness for the front cell is 150 nm and the optimal thickness for the back cell is 90 nm, resulting in a maximum predicted Jsc of 11.8 mA cm−2.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: How does the thickness of the PNDIT-F3N:PEI/PEDOT:PSS interconnecting layer affect the overall device performance?
qa_pairs.answer: The interconnecting layer exhibits thickness insensitivity, which is beneficial for large-area fabrication. The tandem device maintains a high PCE of 11.3% even when the total ICL thickness is increased to 140 nm (with PEDOT:PSS at 70 nm).
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer

qa_pairs.question: Why does a tandem device using only pure PNDIT-F3N in the interconnecting layer exhibit an S-shaped J-V curve?
qa_pairs.answer: An S-shaped J-V curve occurs with pure PNDIT-F3N due to a large energy barrier between the front cell active layer and the modified PEDOT:PSS. This barrier leads to inefficient electron extraction and subsequent hole accumulation at the interface, hindering charge recombination.
qa_pairs.source_title: Highly Efficient Tandem Organic Solar Cell Enabled by Environmentally Friendly Solvent Processed Polymeric Interconnecting Layer
